inputs: issue #2129 body and maintainer reply (github.com page, fetched 2026-11-14)
prompt:
You are the prosecutor. Your job is to FALSIFY the claims below. For each claim, either:
(a) state a concrete scenario in which it is false, AND propose a minimal test or command
    that would demonstrate it; or (b) state you could not falsify it.
You may also raise NEW hypotheses about behaviour the change silently alters.
Every hypothesis must cite exact diff lines. No confidence numbers.
note: Executed attacks carry result and result_detail; the others are hypotheses only.

attacks.scenario: The generated formatter diverges from the built-in contractless resolver for attribute-bearing members ([IgnoreDataMember], [DataMember(Name=)]).
attacks.test_sketch: Probe2129Tests.DataMemberAttributes: serialize ProbeDmType with the generated resolver and ContractlessStandardResolver and compare JSON.
attacks.result_detail: Equal output. Both write Secret and ignore the DataMember rename; see runs/2129/probe/DataMemberAttributes.txt.

attacks.scenario: Public members with no setter or a private setter vanish from the wire format without any diagnostic.
attacks.result_detail: Output is {"Id":1}; Name, PrivSet and Internal are absent and the build reports nothing.

attacks.scenario: Two partial formatters for the same type, or a generated formatter for a [MessagePackObject] type, leave one formatter without a body.
attacks.test_sketch: Probe2129Dup.cs: ProbeDupFormatterA and B for ProbeDupType, and ProbeAttrTypeFormatter for a [MessagePackObject] type.
attacks.result_detail: Build fails with CS0535 on ProbeDupFormatterB and ProbeAttrTypeFormatter; no MsgPack diagnostic names the conflict. See runs/2129/probe/probe-dup.log.

attacks.scenario: init-only and required members break deserialization of the generated formatter.
attacks.result_detail: Round trip passes and wire output equals ContractlessStandardResolver.

attacks.scenario: A hand-written formatter that is also decorated with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] by mistake is excluded from the resolver and also fails MsgPack020, hiding the real mistake.
attacks.test_sketch: Roslyn test with the attribute on a class that has a full hand-written body; expect exactly one diagnostic.

attacks.scenario: The README says nothing needs to be added to the library that owns T, but a struct or class that has only a parameterized constructor is rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor, so a common library shape is unsupported.
attacks.test_sketch: Roslyn test: external type with only a ctor taking arguments; expect the existing MsgPack diagnostic at the formatter.

citations.quote: - Deserialization uses an accessible parameterless constructor (any struct can be created without one).
